newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan caretaker premier promises free elections.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan caretaker premier promises free elections.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid, named by President Farooq Leghari in place of dismissed prime minister Benazir Bhutto, said on Tuesday his priority would be to hold free and fair elections.

"Our first priority will be to hold free, fair and impartial elections," he told reporters at his Islamabad residence, shortly before he was due to go to the presidential palace to take his oath of office.
"It is a very big test and responsibility," the 80-year-old political veteran said. "And God willing, I will try to fulfill this responsibility according to the best of my ability."
"It's a test of my honesty and sense of justice and I pray to God that I may succeed in this," he said.

Khalid, a former parliament speaker who is now rector of the International Islamic University in Islamabad, said free and fair elections could not be held unless the election commission was "powerful and independent".

Khalid, wearing a simple suit, said Leghari had telephoned him at 1.30 a.m. (2030 GMT Monday) to tell him he had been appointed caretaker prime minister and charged with supervising elections to be held on February 3, 1997.
